description: Zentrix Labs (R&D wing of Zentrix Edge) is led by Aariz Mehdi, a Software & AI Engineer (4+ yrs AI/RAG, 2 yrs Full-Stack Next.js/Python). We’re tackling "Flame in Freefall" by building PyroZero—an AI dashboard turning NASA microgravity fire data into spacecraft safety insights. Full-stack & AI code is 100% covered! Join us if you bring skills in NASA Data Research, Physics/Science Writing, Pitch Decks, or Video Editing to help us win a Global Award!
summary: We developed PyroZero, an interactive web application that transforms NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion database into a mission-ready fire safety simulator and decision-support tool for spacecraft engineers. It addresses the "Flame in Freefall" challenge by unifying 15 orbital and planned lunar fire investigations into an automated trade-study ranker, pairing them with a partial-gravity flammability simulator that models flame spread, limiting oxygen concentrations, and virtual NASA-STD-6001B material screening across orbital (0g), Lunar (0.165g), and Martian (0.38g) atmospheres, alongside an evidence-locked advisor and Earth spinoff explorer. This is critical because future Artemis and Mars habitats will use reduced-pressure, high-oxygen air (34% O2 at 8.2 psia) where 70% of standard spacecraft materials fail fire safety tests, yet engineers currently lack direct partial-gravity fire data and must manually search terabytes of isolated ISS files to prevent fatal cabin fires.
details:
What PyroZero Does & How It Works

PyroZero bridges the critical gap between NASA’s 12-terabyte Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository and practical spacecraft habitat engineering across four workspace modules:

1. PSI Mission Explorer (MCDA Trade-Study Matrix):

Engineers select a canonical mission profile—ISS Transit (0g, 101.3 kPa, 21% O2), Artemis Lunar Surface Habitat (0.165g, 56.5 kPa, 34% O2), Mars Surface Habitat (0.38g, 56.5 kPa, 34% O2), or EVA Spacesuit Loop (0.165g, 29.6 kPa, 85–100% O2 proxy)—and customize AHP criteria weights. PyroZero dynamically scores and ranks 15 PSI/ISS investigation groups (12 completed orbital campaigns including BASS-II, Saffire I–VI, SoFIE, ACME CFI-G, E-FIELD, BRE, Flame Design, CLD/SPICE/SLICE, FLEX, SAME, DAFT, plus planned lunar payloads FM2 and LUCI) across Prevention, Detection, and Suppression pillars.

2. Partial-g Flammability Lab & Virtual NASA-STD-6001B Screener:

To address the missing partial-gravity dataset gap in PSI, PyroZero implements a deterministic physics surrogate model grounded in Grashof-Reynolds mixed-convection scaling (U_m, Gr, Re_eff, Damköhler number Da) and ACME E-FIELD Flames Chattock ion-drag equivalent gravity (g_eff). Users adjust continuous sliders for gravity (0g to 1g), electric field (0 to 2.5 kV/cm), pressure (29.6 to 202.6 kPa), oxygen concentration (13% to 85% O2), and ventilation flow (0 to 65 cm/s) across six spacecraft materials (Cast PMMA, SIBAL fabric, Nomex HT90-40, Velcro Nylon, PTFE Teflon, and Beta Cloth/PBI). The workbench renders the live "Check-Mark" Limiting Oxygen Concentration (LOC) boundary curve, quantifies the Negative Oxygen Margin of Safety (NOMS) where Earth 1g upward screening is non-conservative, visualizes 2D flame morphology (aspect ratio and soot/color index), and runs a virtual 30 cm NASA-STD-6001B Test 1 screen with automated JSC 29353D countermeasure prescriptions.

3. Historical Space Fire Forensics & Earth Spinoff Workbench:

Maps root-cause telemetry from Apollo 1 (1967), Apollo 13 (1970), Mir Space Station (1997), and the Artemis II Orion smoke detector anomaly directly to simulator scenarios, alongside terrestrial technology transfers: ISS Fine Water Mist Portable Fire Extinguishers (28–46 um droplets) for cleanrooms and lithium-ion fires, SAME/DAFT 650nm polarimetric dust-discriminating smoke detectors for underground mines, and Apollo-derived 4,500-psi composite SCBA tanks and PBI/Beta-cloth firefighter gear.

4. Citation-Grounded Hybrid GraphRAG Copilot:

Executes a 3-stage server pipeline: (Stage 1) 2-hop traversal across a 67-node, 87-edge in-memory knowledge graph of PSI investigations, materials, and 18 verified NASA knowledge cards; (Stage 2) deterministic server-side execution of the partial-gravity physics engine; and (Stage 3) citation-locked synthesis (supporting live LLM streaming with automatic deterministic fallback) so every engineering recommendation is backed by clickable PSI/DOI/NTRS identifiers.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & Full-Stack Framework: Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas / SVG scientific plots.

- Physics & Retrieval Engine: Deterministic TypeScript surrogate physics engine (pyrozero-engine.ts), in-memory Hybrid GraphRAG engine, Server-Sent Events (SSE) API route (/api/copilot), optional DeepSeek API integration.

- Quality Assurance & Dev Tools: Vitest (114 automated unit/integration tests verifying 3,456 bounded physics states against NASA Saffire-II, Saffire-VI, and BASS-II benchmarks), Playwright browser verification, and OpenAI Codex for code implementation and testing assistance.
